external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: A supplier who uploads their own compliance paperwork.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: portal vendor
external_entities.description: Hosts the portal and pushes the nightly extract; we run no part of it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier portal
processes.description: Vendor-hosted SaaS product suppliers upload to and category managers review in.
processes.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product.
processes.notes: The datasheet's phrases — secure by design, enterprise-grade encryption throughout, fully authenticated and audited, fully compliant — name no technology and state no verifiable control, so none of them set an attribute here.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: Loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket and writes supplier records.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: document store
data_stores.description: Where the uploaded compliance documents rest, inside the vendor's platform.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_stores.notes: Enterprise-grade encryption throughout is a vendor marketing claim about the platform, not a stated property of this store, so encryption_at_rest is unknown rather than encrypted.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: Bucket in our cloud account the vendor pushes the nightly extract into.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: Holds the supplier records loaded from the nightly extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

data_flows.name: upload documents
data_flows.description: Supplier uploads compliance paperwork to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
data_flows.authentication: username and password issued by the vendor
data_flows.data_description: insurance certificates, food safety audits, and supplier staff contact details

data_flows.name: review documents
data_flows.description: Category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and records an approval or rejection.
data_flows.source_excerpt: review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it
data_flows.notes: All access is fully authenticated and audited is a datasheet claim covering the platform generally; the source states how suppliers sign in and never states how category managers do, so this stays unknown.

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The portal puts uploaded documents into the vendor platform's store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: push nightly extract
data_flows.description: The vendor initiates a nightly push of the supplier data extract into our bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source contradicts itself here: we were told the extract is encrypted end to end, and the landing bucket runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV picked up as-is. Neither statement is privileged over the other and nothing in the source resolves them, so this is unknown rather than either encrypted or unencrypted, and the conflict is itself a finding.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service picks the extract file up from the bucket as-is.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is

data_flows.name: write supplier records
data_flows.description: The service writes the loaded records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: Where suppliers sit when they upload their paperwork.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: vendor platform
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor's hosting, holding the portal and the documents; we run no part of it and can verify nothing inside it.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: Our own cloud account, holding the landing bucket, the supplier master service and the supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: Suppliers reach the portal across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The portal is a vendor-hosted SaaS product suppliers sign in to, and the source places suppliers nowhere on our networks.
